name: harvest-project-to-zapier-table

trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger — no webhook_url, and none expected. Polling triggers never backfill, so the Harvest projects that existed before this version was published will not be logged; the table was reconciled by hand at migration time instead (see backfill below). The classic Zap carried polling_interval_override: 0 (the default), so nothing was lost by durables not exposing an interval.

connections_note: Harvest supplies the trigger only; the workflow body binds no connection. Title: "Harvest dennis@work.flowers : Company Flow Pte. Ltd. (dba Work.Flowers".

connectionless_apps.TableCLIAPI: find_record / create_record / update_record — Zapier Tables auth is automatic, no connection and no task cost

tables.01K8A2KV9X1W95GAB6Y69D7G4C: Harvest Projects (New) — f1 project_id, f2 client_id, f3 is_active, f4 Name, f5 Project Page ID. Shared with notion-project-to-harvest-client-project (writes f5) and read by start-a-timer-from-notion-task on (f5, f3=true).

migration.from: classic Zap "Add Harvest Project to Zapier Table"
changes: Blind create -> UPSERT on f1 (project_id). Confirmed with Dennis 2026-08-07. The classic Zap always created a row, so every project created from a Notion Projects page got two: one from the Notion Zap (with f5) and one from this Harvest poll ~30s later. 16 such pairs existed.

is_active read defensively, defaulting to TRUE when absent. The classic Zap's {{=gives[...]['is_active']}} recorded false on all 16 duplicates, including projects whose Notion-side twin (written 30s earlier) said true — an unresolved template coerces to false, and false is the dangerous direction because start-a-timer-from-notion-task gates on f3=true.
f5 is never written or cleared here. Verified 2026-08-07 on a scratch row that update_record leaves unlisted fields untouched: f1 and f5 both survived an update of f2/f3/f4 only.

backfill_2026_08_07.note: One-off reconciliation done at migration time, approved by Dennis after the time-tracking consequence was spelled out and reaffirmed.
backfill_2026_08_07.result: 66 rows -> 50, no duplicate project_ids, 0 rows disagreeing with Harvest.
backfill_2026_08_07.consequence: All 15 flips were true -> false. Only 3 Harvest projects are active (48185265 DEAL-40 Knoxx, 47968437 DEAL-53 Terrascope, 46733152 DEAL-35 SCW) and none is mapped to a Notion Projects page. start-a-timer-from-notion-task previously matched 20 rows on (f5, f3=true); it now matches 6, and all 6 are junk — three carry a project CODE in f1 instead of an id (WF-10, WF-17, WF-20, written by the classic Notion Zap's step 8), two reference Harvest projects since deleted, one is a blank row. In practice the Notion Track Time button can no longer resolve a project. Flagged to Dennis before the re-sync; he reaffirmed. Open question worth its own look: Notion Projects are archived in Harvest while time is billed to the DEAL-* retainers, so the Projects -> Harvest mapping may be the wrong axis for time tracking.

verified_paths: upsert onto an existing row (project 48549718) -> action 'updated', run 019fda54-ef95-7120-8663-79ea078acfd9. NOTE: it matched the DUPLICATE row (01KVJKAYDFDSM5AE270YR67M25) rather than the page-id-carrying one, because two rows then shared that project_id — which is exactly why the dedupe was a prerequisite, not cosmetics. That row has since been deleted.
update_record preserves unlisted fields (f1, f5) — scratch row 01KZD589DSFSND4TFH06F2Q7H8, created, updated on f2/f3/f4 only, read back, deleted
verification.unverified: The create-project-row branch (a Harvest project with no existing row) has not run, and no real new_project trigger delivery has been observed — so the exact key the trigger uses for the project id is still inferred from the classic Zap's output (record_id, with id/project_id as fallbacks). The first genuinely new Harvest project is the first live test of both.
